column3: The Hebrew gives the platter’s weight as “one hundred and thirty,” without explicitly repeating “shekels” for that first weight; BSB supplies the unit.
The Hebrew gives “ten gold” without an explicit weighing verb or the word “shekels”; BSB says “weighing ten shekels.”
The Hebrew calls the bull “a son of the herd” and the lamb “a son of its year”; BSB gives “young bull” and “a year old.”
